newsitem.title: UK: CWS spokesman says to proceed with legal action.
newsitem.headline: CWS spokesman says to proceed with legal action.

text.p: Britain's Co-operative Wholesale Society (CWS) said on Thursday it had had no formal confirmation from predator Galileo that the group no longer proposed to make a bid for the mutually-owned society.

"There has been no formal communication (from Galileo) with the CWS this morning," a CWS spokesman told Reuters when asked if the CWS had received notification that Galileo would not be pursuing its proposal. "As it stands the legal action (against Galileo and various other parties) goes ahead tomorrow," he added.
CWS spokesman says to proceed with legal action=2

Earlier Galileo Group, the special bidding vehicle set up by entrepreneur Andrew Regan to bid for CWS, said it would not pursue its bid after the CWS chairman rejected its invitation to put its plans to CWS members.
"In the light of this response, Galileo announces that it will not be pursuing its proposal," the group said in a statement.
Regan has been stalking the mutually-owned Co-op for several months but an expected 1.2 billion pound ($1.9 billion) bid was thwarted by CWS legal action.

Galileo's announcement followed a high-profile defence by CWS involving a High Court injunction to prevent the predator from using confidential information obtained from a now suspended Co-op senior manager and CWS making its concerns about a payment in a previous deal with Regan known to Britain's Serious Fraud Office.

The 153-year-old CWS has interests ranging from supermarkets and funeral parlours to the profitable Co-operative Bank and a large insurance arm. Galileo, an offshoot of 31-year-old Regan's Guernsey-based investment trust Lanica, had the backing of several City institutions as well as Japanese securities firm Nomura.

Despite its poorly performing retail business, CWS has consistently rejected any suggestion of selling any of its businesses to Regan or anyone else. The group's complex structure has also been seen as a major barrier to any hostile takeover.
Although it had never made a formal offer for the CWS, Galileo said it wanted to propose turning it into a limited company and then offering to buy the group.
But there has been widespread speculation that CWS is now "in play" with other parties interested in taking over parts of its varied empire. No other bidders have yet emerged.
